river_name: Tungabhadra River & Krishna River (Sacred Confluence / Tungabhadra–Krishna Sangam)

ghats.name: Jogulamba River Ghat
ghats.description: Located on the banks of the adjacent Tungabhadra River, this area is structured with steps and safety railings for devotees wishing to take a traditional holy purification bath before prayers. Dedicated separate changing enclosures for men and women are available directly near the river bathing points.

ghats.name: Alampur Pushkar Ghat
ghats.description: Sacred river bank steps looking over the Krishna and Tungabhadra confluence (0.5 km from temple).

safety_rules: Bathe only within designated barricaded zones along the steps.
Do not cross safety chain railings due to strong river currents.
Children and senior citizens must be accompanied by adults near the water edge.
significance: The Tungabhadra ghats near Alampur are used by devotees for holy bathing and religious observances, particularly on auspicious occasions and during major pilgrimage periods. Key river events include: 1. Theppotsavam (Float Festival): Celebrated as part of Sharannavaratri/Dasara celebrations on Vijayadashami, where processional deities are taken on a decorated float at the Tungabhadra–Krishna Sangam near Alampur. 2. Tungabhadra Pushkaralu: Major river festival held once every 12 years when Jupiter enters the zodiac sign associated with the Tungabhadra Pushkaram cycle (last held 20 Nov to 1 Dec 2020, next in 2032). 3. Krishna & Tungabhadra Pushkaralu: Millions of pilgrims travel to take a holy dip in the river confluence to wash away sins before offering prayers to the Goddess.
